svg.title: Glider: purple classification after both orange layers
svg.text: Next: purple tiles classify the packed total
Nine supplied bits in; one of three logical output classes: 3, 4, or other. The count includes the centre.
Complete the second orange layer first. Circle = 0; plus = 1; circle + plus socket = either bit.
Purple output badges below are signal labels; their physical connector profiles are not yet specified.
Top-left 3 × 3 in each target cell: nine ordinary bit outputs.
C ports remain outside the purple footprint, at their existing heights.
Highlighted cell: five ones are enough to select “other”
The other four sockets accept 0 or 1.
All nine sockets still need a connector.
This tile therefore recognizes a total of 5 or more.
Three output classes feed the black/white layer:
3: live for either centre state. 4: live only for C1. Other: dead for either centre state.
The original centre travels separately on the right-hand C column; it is not replaced by the count.
Colours identify layers. Connector shape, not colour, will distinguish the three purple output signals.
